questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more stopping power than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Keep your speed the same or go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden movements. Stay out of the center of the lane and follow tire tracks left by other vehicles. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: For a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to protect against wind, cold, and rain.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect against wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit riding to no more than 6 hours per day. Take a rest break at least every 2 hours. Avoid stimulants because fatigue will be worse when they wear off.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance does a motorcycle need?
questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a car.
questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs the same distance to stop as a car.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you away from blind spots, wind blasts, and hazards. Your position should discourage sharing and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: To swerve quickly, you should:

options.text: Push the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side you want to go. To turn left, push the left grip, then the right to straighten. To turn right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: In good conditions, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least 2 seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow me.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on either side increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because drivers will see you easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check side mirrors.
Is recommended because passengers may alert the driver.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you.

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color is the lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, you should instruct a passenger to do all of the following except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit close to you, not far away. They should mount after the engine starts, sit far forward without crowding you, hold onto the handholds or your waist, and keep their legs away from hot and moving parts.

questions.question: When stopped, which gear should you stay in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Should remain in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is following you too closely?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow to warn the other driver.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn a tailgater. The driver behind you may not see hazards ahead that require you to slow down.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Nearly 40 percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking. Alcohol is a major cause of serious and fatal motorcycle accidents.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle?

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: Apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As you brake, more weight moves forward, giving the front wheel more grip. Gradually increase front brake pressure while reducing rear brake pressure. Keep your knees against the tank and eyes up to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Abruptly apply both brakes while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: First straighten your motorcycle and square the handlebars, then stop. If you cannot straighten up, apply brakes smoothly and gradually while reducing your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that make it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars where there is better grip. Reduce your speed on wet surfaces.

questions.question: How do you get maximum straight-line braking power?

options.text: Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Maximum straight-line braking happens when you fully apply both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, how should you do it?

options.text: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press the front brake hard to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down safely. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from everything below, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Your riding clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. They should also help protect you in a crash.

questions.question: How should you choose your lane position?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change positions based on different conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change positions based on different conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Position yourself where you are most visible to other drivers and where you have space around you.

questions.question: In a group of riders, who should set the speed?
questions.correctAnswerText: The last rider
questions.explanation: The last rider in the group should set the speed. This ensures that no one gets left behind.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This way they won't fall behind, and more experienced riders can watch them from behind.
